title: Can the system dynamics remain structurally non-Markovian while its experimentally accessible memory signatures disappear?
authors: Sayan Sengupta, Anish Sharma, George Biswas, Anindya Biswas
abstract: We investigate how unresolved quasistatic disorder in system bath coupling affects non-Markovian dynamics in spin environments. The coupling is fixed within each experimental shot but varies between shots, so repeated shot tomography reconstructs a disorder averaged dynamical map. For a single spin bath with pure dephasing Ising interaction, disorder can drive a transition to CP-divisible dynamics for fixed bath preparations, with a critical strength set by bath polarization along the interaction axis. However, when the bath state fluctuates physically between shots, the averaged dynamics remain CP indivisible at any finite disorder strength. We extend these results analytically to inhomogeneously coupled pure dephasing baths of any number \(N\) of non-interacting spins. At any finite disorder strength, one unpolarized bath spin suffices to retain CP-indivisible dynamics, whereas a fully polarized bath yields Markovian (CP-divisible) dynamics. Dynamics with physically fluctuating bath states likewise remain non-Markovian (CP indivisible) at finite disorder for arbitrary \(N\) in the pure dephasing case. For anisotropic Heisenberg interactions, any nonzero transverse exchange eliminates the disorder driven transition to CP divisibility in a single spin bath. Exact diagonalization of anisotropic models with inhomogeneous couplings up to \(N=12\) reveals persistent trace distance revivals for fixed bath preparations, sampled Haar random preparations, and physically fluctuating bath states, showing that this effect of transverse exchange extends beyond a single bath spin. Increasing disorder still suppresses experimentally accessible revivals and can make memory effects unresolvable at finite measurement resolution even as the dynamics remain CP indivisible. Thus, transverse exchange and physical bath state fluctuations preserve dynamical indivisibility against unresolved coupling disorder.
summary: This theoretical study examines the robustness of non-Markovian quantum dynamics when the coupling to the environment is subject to unresolved disorder. The authors demonstrate that while disorder can make memory effects unresolvable, structural non-Markovianity can persist if the bath state physically fluctuates or if transverse interactions are present. This has implications for interpreting experimental measurements in open quantum systems.
main_problem: The paper investigates whether a quantum system's dynamics can retain structural non-Markovianity (CP indivisibility) even when the memory effects are suppressed or become unresolvable due to unresolved quasi-static disorder in the system-bath coupling.
main_result: Transverse exchange interactions and physical fluctuations of the bath state are shown to preserve dynamical indivisibility against coupling disorder, even when memory signatures are suppressed.
method: The analysis uses process tomography to reconstruct disorder-averaged dynamical maps and employs the criterion of CP divisibility to characterize Markovianity, extending results analytically to multiple bath spins.
model_or_system: The model involves an open quantum system (spin qubit) coupled to a bath of spins. The coupling is subjected to quasi-static disorder, and the analysis compares different averaging procedures (fixed vs. fluctuating bath states).
key_observables: CP divisibility (for Markovianity), coherence revivals, and the $\ell_1$-norm of coherence.
important_parameters: Disorder strength ($\epsilon$), bath polarization, and the presence/absence of transverse exchange coupling.
main_assumptions: The disorder is assumed to be quasi-static, and the analysis focuses on the divisibility of the disorder-averaged dynamical map.
figures_summary: Not specified, but the notes detail complex mathematical derivations involving multiple substitutions and transformations to evaluate integrals related to coherence measures.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first analyzing the pure dephasing case with disorder, then generalizing to $N$ spins, introducing anisotropic Heisenberg interactions, and finally discussing the implications of physical bath state fluctuations.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the crucial experimental challenge of distinguishing true structural non-Markovianity from apparent Markovian behavior caused by measurement limitations or environmental averaging.
